title: Shrouded Sky - Patch Notes 1.17.0
body:
# Shrouded Sky - Patch Notes 1.17.0

Attention Raiders!

Fierce hurricanes are now tearing across the surface, bringing new demands for fighting through poor visibility, strong winds, and flying debris. Scouts have identified two new ARC types roaming the Rust Belt; stay alert while the storms pass through, but those who can read the weather correctly may find chances hidden within the turmoil.

# What's New?

* Hurricane Map Condition

* Two New ARC Enemies

* The Weather Monitoring System - Seasonal Player Project

* Free Raider Deck

* Dam Battlegrounds Map Update

* Expedition Window

* Facial Hair Customization

# Patch Highlights

* Weapon balancing changes affecting Stitcher, Kettle, Venator, Jupiter and Aphelion.

* A piano has been added as an object players can interact with in the world.

* Turning on every NVIDIA Freestyle filter at once is now blocked, removing an unfair visual edge.

* Players can now reroll Feats up to three times daily at no cost.

* PvP Feats have been removed, some existing Feats were updated, and several new ones were introduced.

* Ziplines can no longer be attached to carryable objects.

* Mines, traps, and remote flares can no longer be set down on top of other deployables.

# Balance Changes

## Weapons

Update 1.13 included a fix meant to optimize our weapons, but it unexpectedly lowered the overall fire-rate of semi-automatic weapons. We reversed that fix in 1.13.1, but that update introduced a different problem that was never intended.

Many players reported what felt like a "shadow buff" to weapons. After looking into it, we discovered 1.13.1 had unintentionally affected our weapon input buffers. Previously, players needed to time their inputs to match a weapon's intended firing cadence to get its full potential. After 1.13.1, players could simply spam-click instead, skipping the skill needed to learn that cadence. We want to preserve some of that skill element, but we also acknowledge that the earlier system did not feel responsive enough. To strike a better balance, we've built additional tools to control the input buffering window for each weapon individually, and adjusted the semi-automatic weapons using these tools. Spam-clicking will still fire the weapon responsively, but players who pace their shots deliberately will get better results.

We've also been examining the balance between low tier and high tier weapons. Many of you have raised concerns that certain low tier weapons perform better than higher tier ones despite costing far less. We want to shift that balance somewhat while still allowing skilled players some room to outperform their weapon's tier. We're beginning by lowering the overall time-to-kill (TTK) for the Stitcher and Kettle, and boosting the maneuverability of the Aphelion and Jupiter. We're also revisiting the Venator, which continues to dominate many PvP fights.

**Dev Note:** The Stitcher has served well as a close-range weapon rewarding smart positioning, but its fast TTK sometimes results in players being ambushed and killed with little time to respond. Many of you pointed to its high headshot damage as a major cause. Body-shot TTK is generally fine, but when enough shots land on the head at close range, TTK becomes noticeably faster than other weapons. These adjustments bring headshot TTK closer in line with body-shot TTK, by reducing full-spray accuracy and lowering the headshot multiplier.

* Headshot Multiplier reduced from 2.5 to 1.75

* Base Damage reduced from 7 to 6.5

* Per Shot Dispersion increased by roughly 50% (bloom occurs faster)

**Dev Note:** The Kettle has occupied an odd spot. Its high damage was designed for more deliberate use at medium range, but many players use it up close, effectively as an SMG. We want to separate it more clearly from the Stitcher while preserving the versatility players enjoy. We are lowering base damage to bring its TTK closer in line, while keeping the high headshot multiplier to encourage players to aim for headshots.

* Base Damage reduced from 10 to 8.5

**Dev Note:** Since the Venator's nerf in 1.3.0, we've continued monitoring its performance. Many of you have flagged that it still dominates PvP, and our data confirms it remains one of the strongest weapons currently in the game. We want weapons at this tier to perform well, but not to this extreme. We are reducing its damage to lower its TTK, and may look at ammo consumption and cost-efficiency further if needed.

* Headshot Multiplier reduced from 2.5 to 2

* Base Damage reduced from 9 to 8

**Dev Note:** In PvP, the Jupiter deals the highest headshot damage of any weapon, but landing headshots at range is difficult. Using it up close is also risky, since a missed shot leaves you exposed until you reload or switch weapons. We are increasing ADS zoom to help you land shots on target, and reducing equip and unequip times to make it easier to follow up with a secondary weapon.

* ADS Magnification improved from approximately 1.9x to approximately 2.2x

* Equip Time improved from 1.2s to 1.05s

* Unequip Time improved from 0.9s to 0.75s

**Dev Note:** We were not satisfied with the Aphelion's previous balance. It was meant to be a PvP-focused legendary weapon, but it couldn't match the pace of other PvP weapons. We've adjusted it to feel lighter and more agile, improving its viability in PvP.

* Base Reload Time reduced from 4.5s to 3.5s

* Time Between Shots reduced from 0.9s to 0.7s

* Vertical Recoil reduced by approximately 50%

* ADS Settle Speed improved by approximately 35%

## Item and Crafting

* This item is now available by default at the Workbench.

The following item values and costs have been adjusted, along with appropriate changes to recycle and salvage outputs:

* **Deadline**

* Value increased from 5,000 to 6,000.

* Trader price increased from 15,000 to 18,000.

* A new ARC part has been added as a crafting requirement.

* **Trailblazer**

* Value increased from 1,600 to 2,200.

* Trader price increased from 4,800 to 6,600.

* A new ARC part has been added as a crafting requirement.

* **Wolfpack**

* Value increased from 5,000 to 6,000.

* Rocketeer Driver added as a crafting requirement.

* Refined Explosive cost reduced.

* **Vita Spray**

* Value increased from 3,000 to 3,400.

* Tick Pod added as a crafting requirement.

* **Showstopper**

* Value decreased from 2,200 to 2,100.

* Hornet Driver added as a crafting requirement.

* Crafting component changed from Advanced Electrical Components to Electrical Components.

* ARC Parts sell values have been lowered to better reflect how they're used in crafting and progression.

# Content and Bug Fixes

## Achievements

* Fixed an issue causing the "Blindsided" achievement to sometimes fail to trigger on the first attempt.

## Animation

* Fixed several animation issues that occurred while vaulting.

* Fixed an issue where certain weapons did not visibly drop their magazine during reloads.

* Fixed an issue where reattaching to a ladder after jumping could distort the climbing animation.

* Refined equip animations for pistols and the hand cannon so their timing matches better, reducing visual popping when switching from being unarmed.

* Improved arm and weapon positioning during shoulder swaps to prevent visual popping during the transition.

* Fixed an issue where fall damage was not applied if the player was in a knockback animation.

* Refined low-health reaction animations for better clarity.

* Fixed the weapon-shake animation incorrectly triggering indoors during freezing weather; it now only triggers outdoors.

## ARC

* Fixed an issue where Surveyors and Fireballs could open before fully stabilizing.

* Reduced erratic movement of ARC parts when attached to a looted item.

* Hornets now retain their upper armor after being destroyed, making the lootable piece easier to tell apart from Wasps.

* Fixed an issue where the Rocketeer would sometimes fail to fire despite having a clear shot at its target.

* Reduced instances where the Sentinel's shots could pass through geometry when its weapon clips into walls at very close range.

## Audio

* Limited the number of bullet sound effects per trigger pull on burst weapons to match burst size, preventing extra shots from playing.

* Reduced audio stuttering on lower-spec PCs for smoother, more consistent sound.

* Lowered non-radio voice volumes, including in-game dialogue.

* Fixed an issue where sliding on stairs or debris could cause audio stutters.

* Scrappy will now cluck less often, based on player feedback about excessive noise.

* Reduced overall volume and rebalanced the menu sound effects and music mix for a more comfortable experience in Speranza.

* Shortened one tube deployment music track that played for too long during sessions.

* Birds perched on ziplines now screech with correct positional audio when startled.

* Slightly decreased audio occlusion and obstruction overall, especially for players.

* Updated the acoustic guitar music tracks.

## Cosmetics

* The Volare Set

* The Surgeon Set

* The Devotee Set is coming soon.

* Added a new facial hair customization option.

* Fixed an incorrect visor glass material on the green color variant of the Marco outfit.

* Fixed multiple instances of clipping on certain outfits.

## Gameplay

* Added a piano as an interactable object in the world.

* Fixed an issue that allowed interactions to be triggered from too far away, letting players open doors, activate hatches, or loot items without being nearby.

* Hold and continuous interactions now cancel if the player equips a different item or weapon.

* Fixed an issue where players could become unable to move after being revived with a defib.

* Prevented players from standing on or being carried by thrown grenades or other non-walkable items.

* Added missing gamepad aim assist for Sentinels, Turrets, Shredders, and Surveyors.

* Disabled queuing for the Practice Range while in a party, preventing matchmaking errors.

* Fixed an issue where a downed raider's body could block hatch extraction by triggering a search prompt.

* Turning on every NVIDIA Freestyle filter simultaneously is now blocked, removing an unfair visual edge.

* Purchases using seeds or free loadout augments can now be made even when the stash is overflowing.

## General

* General performance improvements.

* Fixed several popping issues.

* Fixed a crash that occurred when launching the game with DirectX 11.

* Fixed a crash that could occur while traversing ziplines.

## Maps

* Fixed broken interactions near the top of certain ladders.

* Fixed missing collision on several environment props, reducing clipping and unintended traversal.

* General lighting fixes applied across different maps.

* The chance of finding rare loot in chimneys has been slightly lowered during the Bird City map condition.

* Fixed multiple collision issues on Stella Montis (Lobby, Atrium, Loading Bay, Train Station tunnels, Seed Vault) that let players reach out-of-bounds areas via the 'Unstuck' function, and addressed shots originating from the Lobby ceiling.

* Adjusted night lighting on Stella Montis to improve visibility in darker areas.

* Improved night-time visibility at the Seed Vault extraction point by adding local lighting.

* Fixed an issue where lowered Spillway bridges still showed an interaction prompt; the interaction is now correctly disabled once the bridge is down.

* Fixed an issue that let players climb on top of metro trains.

* Improved thunderstorm lighting for better visual clarity.

* Fixed an issue that allowed players to go out of bounds in the Blue Gate tunnels.

## Movement

* Adjusted ladder jump-off behavior to match vault jump-off behavior, smoothing movement and preventing unintended momentum from rapid inputs.

* Fixed an issue where sliding could clip through stairs and escalators.

## Progression

* Feats can now be rerolled up to three times per day for free.

* PvP Feats have been removed, some existing Feats were updated, and new ones were added.

* Added an Expedition catch-up system letting players earn missed Skill Points from previous runs, along with an updated UI to track progress.

* Fixed an issue where players occasionally did not receive a skill point despite it being shown on the result screen.

* Candleberries found in Blue Gate now count toward the Harvest Plants trial.

## Quests

* Added clearer ping labels for quest-related world objects to improve readability.

* Fixed an issue where the next objective pop-up in multi-step quests could be missing or show a step that was already completed. It now consistently shows the correct upcoming objective.

* Fixed an issue where a quest item could appear as world loot even when the related quest wasn't active.

## Social

* When playing in a party, map selection now shows all locations unlocked by whichever member has played the most rounds.

* Fixed an issue where previous teammates could still appear in the Social tab's In Proximity list after starting a new session.

* Added clearer error messages for failed friend requests caused by too many outgoing requests or rate limiting.

* Fixed an issue where friends appeared offline when they had more than one platform linked.

* Added the ability to hide friend requests.

## UI

* Item pings for items inside containers now appear above the container's interaction point instead of showing at the wrong location in certain containers.

* Added a ready-up warning when deploying with Raider Hatch keys into a map that has no active hatches.

* Added icons to inventory tooltips showing recycle and salvage outputs.

* Fixed an issue where squad colors could display incorrectly after squad changes.

* Fixed a bug where adding a secondary keybind would overwrite the primary keybind in the next round.

* Updated localization for unique loot dropped by new enemy variants to improve in-game naming and clarity.

* Improved matchmaking messaging when some party members are still topside.

* Fixed an issue where end-of-round health was not displayed correctly for all players.

* It is now clearer, when joining a party while in Speranza, which party member is currently topside.

* Players can now use the mouse scroll wheel to switch between pages in the Raider Deck.

* Polished UI text and updated translations across all supported languages.

* Added further ping labels for various quest objects to improve clarity.

* Fixed an issue where mouse smoothing could remain enabled even after being turned off, ensuring the setting applies correctly at the start of each round.

* Improved the red zipline preview shown when a zipline cannot be placed.

* Updated the login message to clearly explain when access is restricted due to the shared account owner being banned.

* Fixed an issue in Expeditions where the timer could go negative after the departure countdown while the Sign Up button remained active; the screen now updates correctly and disables the button.

* Fixed an issue where the repair preview did not display correctly when repairing items.

* Crafting and recycling screens now show item costs and rewards in a consistent order for easier reading.

* The VoIP icon in the HUD now more clearly shows whether the microphone will transmit when using Push To Talk or Toggle To Talk.

## Utility

* Pop Triggers and Spotter Relays can now be assigned to quick slots.

* The Spotter Relay can now be deployed as a trap that lures nearby ARC.

* The Pop Trigger can now be deployed to roll forward briefly before exploding.

* Added a new Field craft item: the Shaker instrument.

* Adjusted Vita Spray so healing applies continuously during use, preventing exploit cases.

* Fixed unintended behavior in the Snaphook that caused it to pull players even after being cancelled.

* Ziplines can no longer be placed on carryable objects.

* Fixed zipline placement on ARC remnants that could consume the item or leave the zipline only partially placed.

* Mines, traps, and remote flares can no longer be placed on ziplines or other small deployables.

* The T3 Tactical (Healing) Augment description now correctly states that healing is applied instantly.

## VFX

* Fixed an issue where the Jupiter's windup visual could face sideways, making the beam appear misaligned.

* Fixed an issue where the Trailblazer's gas effect could persist indefinitely if interrupted by the Matriarch's shield.

# Known Issues

* The 'Purchase Raider Tokens' page may appear in front of the inbox and profile page when switching between them.

* Player animations may appear broken when a search of the Baron Husk is interrupted.

* Certain containers may be temporarily unavailable for interaction.

* Ziplines placed onto destroyed ARC parts will not display correctly.

* The Scrappy 'Batting Helmet' and the 'Slugger' outfit might not display correctly in the event preview.

* The 'Comparative Study' achievement sometimes fails to progress correctly after damaging the hanging drone dummies.

* The 'Unyielding' achievement/trophy fails to progress on console when knocking out raiders using the associated prompt.

* Unintended visual effects can occasionally appear.

* One of the new ARC enemies occasionally has an unusable interaction when destroyed.

* Flying ARC may sometimes appear stuck in an idle state.

* The Embark ID Discriminator sometimes fails to display.

* Pressing LMB outside the item select area closes the item select window in the Expeditions menu.

# Anti-Cheat

Our previous update on tackling unfair play didn't fully convey how complex and large-scale cheat detection actually is. Our defenses work on multiple levels: some checks are simple and immediate, while others rely on behavioral, data-driven analysis that evolves over time. We also use broad gameplay telemetry and machine learning to identify patterns that aren't obvious at a glance. These methods take longer to build, must be updated as game systems change, and don't always deliver the instant certainty that straightforward software detections do.

We've recently taken action against several exploits and are tightening our rules while stepping up enforcement further. Serious violations now carry stricter penalties. Strong detections will result in immediate permanent bans, while other cases will receive a temporary suspension with a single chance to change behavior. Recent updates to Family Sharing have strengthened our ability to address misconduct and made it easier to remove bad actors from the game. We are also preparing to launch a systematic manual review process for ban appeals. The game is still young and the volume of telemetry is massive, but this process ensures each case gets careful handling as we keep learning quickly and investing heavily in the precision of our enforcement tools.

Our dedicated anti-cheat team works continuously to keep the game fair. It remains an ongoing effort, and we remain committed to it.
